quizzes.title: SCO membership and bodies
quizzes.passage: The SCO brings together a group of countries that sit at the crossroads of Central Asia, South Asia and East Asia. Russia and Iran also take part in its work, which gives the grouping a wide geographical reach. The organisation runs cooperation programmes in several areas, including security, trade, transport and cultural contacts. Its work is spread across a set of bodies, and each body handles a separate part of the agenda. The organisation's leaders meet every year, and the host country for that meeting rotates along with the chairmanship. The organisation marked its 25th anniversary in 2026, and its theme for that year stressed sustainable peace, development and prosperity. Over time, the membership has expanded in stages, and the organisation has brought in new partners as its reach has grown. The SCO also encourages political dialogue among its members and supports exchanges between the peoples of the region. Together, these features show a grouping that combines security concerns with economic and cultural work across a large part of the continent. Its members include several large states, and its meetings give them a regular channel for discussion at the highest political level. One of its stated objectives is to strengthen mutual trust, good-neighbourliness and mutual support on issues of security.

questions.q: In which year did India and Pakistan become full members of the SCO?
questions.explanation: India and Pakistan became full members of the SCO in 2017.

questions.q: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) of the SCO is located in which city?
questions.explanation: RATS is based in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

questions.q: Which of the following countries is an observer state of the SCO?
questions.explanation: Mongolia is one of the two observer states, along with Afghanistan.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The SCO was formally established in Shanghai.
Reason (R): The SCO Charter was signed in 2002.
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the Charter signing in 2002 does not explain the establishment in Shanghai.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Council of Heads of Government   ->   A. Border issues and military confidence-building
II. SCO Secretariat   ->   B. Economic and developmental cooperation
III. Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure   ->   C. Permanent administrative body
IV. Shanghai Five   ->   D. Counter-terrorism cooperation
questions.explanation: The Council of Heads of Government covers economic cooperation, the Secretariat is the permanent body, RATS covers counter-terrorism and the Shanghai Five was set up to address border issues.

questions.q:
Read the statements below about the organisation:
I. The SCO is described as a Permanent Eurasian Inter-Governmental Organisation.
II. Economic and connectivity cooperation is among the SCO's focus areas.
III. The SCO is an inter-governmental military alliance, like the Collective Security Treaty Organisation.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the SCO is not described as a military alliance (the CSTO is).

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. China was one of the countries that created the Shanghai Five.
II. Pakistan is an observer state of the SCO.
III. Tajikistan is an observer state of the SCO.
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since Pakistan and Tajikistan are full members rather than observers.

quizzes.title: SCO structure and timeline
quizzes.passage: The SCO links a broad group of Eurasian states, with members drawn from Central Asia, South Asia, China, Russia and Iran. Its agenda is wide and covers security questions, economic and connectivity projects, political dialogue, and exchanges between cultures and peoples. Leaders gather at an annual summit, and the host role moves to a different member state as the chairmanship rotates. Governance is spread across several bodies, and each has a distinct area of work. The organisation marked its 25th anniversary in 2026, and its theme for that year stressed sustainable peace, development and prosperity. Membership has grown in stages since the early years, with new countries joining at different times. The organisation's cooperation is organised around clear goals, including trust among members, trade and connectivity, and cultural exchange. Taken together, these features describe a platform that brings governments from several parts of the continent into a common framework for cooperation. Its stated objectives include strengthening mutual trust, good-neighbourliness and mutual support on issues of security. The organisation also promotes people-to-people exchange in fields such as culture, education and science. Its cooperation extends to transport and digital economy, as well as environmental protection. Its work on energy is also part of its agenda.

questions.q: Which Uzbek city is home to the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) of the SCO?
questions.explanation: RATS is based in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

questions.q: In which year did India and Pakistan become full members of the SCO?
questions.explanation: India and Pakistan became full members of the SCO in 2017.

questions.q: Which SCO body handles economic and developmental cooperation?
questions.explanation: The Council of Heads of Government handles economic and developmental cooperation.

questions.q: In which city was the SCO formally established on 15 June 2001?
questions.explanation: The SCO was formally established on 15 June 2001 in Shanghai.

questions.q: What is the name of the SCO's permanent administrative body?
questions.explanation: The SCO Secretariat is the permanent administrative body of the organisation.

questions.q: Which two countries are observer states of the SCO?
questions.explanation: Afghanistan and Mongolia are the SCO's two observers.

questions.q: What does the acronym RATS stand for within the SCO?
questions.explanation: RATS is the Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure, which handles counter-terrorism cooperation.

quizzes.title: India's SCO engagement
quizzes.passage: India's engagement with the SCO is part of its wider effort to stay active across the Eurasian region. The grouping gives India a multilateral platform where it can meet Russia and China along with several Central Asian republics. India's stated position is that peace, security and stability in the region matter, and that disputes should be settled through dialogue and diplomacy. It also supports inclusive economic development, and it highlights digital cooperation, energy partnerships and green development. India also emphasises people-to-people contacts and cultural linkages with partners. India condemns terrorism in all its forms and supports zero tolerance against it. India's approach allows it to cooperate on issues where its interests align with others while keeping room for independent choices in other matters. The grouping's stated aims include peace, security, stability, economic cooperation and cultural exchange. Its objectives also include building a just, democratic and rational new international order. The SCO is also described as a platform for cooperation, with a focus on peace, prosperity and sustainable development. The SCO allows issue-based alignment, so partners can cooperate on specific questions while differing on others. Such alignment lets India engage with Russia and China on some matters while pursuing its own position on others.

questions.q: Which port and transport corridor reduce dependence on Pakistan-controlled transit for European and Central Asian trade?
questions.explanation: Chabahar Port and INSTC reduce dependence on Pakistan-controlled transit.

questions.q: Which SCO body treats terror financing and radicalisation as collective regional concerns?
questions.explanation: The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure frames terror financing and radicalisation as collective regional concerns.

questions.q: Through the SCO, India gains institutional access to which group of countries?
questions.explanation: The SCO provides institutional access to Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): India refuses to join the BRI.
Reason (R): CPEC passes through territories that are disputed.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet links India's refusal of the BRI to CPEC passing through disputed territories.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Soft power pillars in India's SCO vision   ->   A. Bishkek
II. Host city of the 6th World Nomad Games 2026   ->   B. Slow progress in payment arrangements and transport corridors
III. Recognition of the Nomad Games initiative   ->   C. Ayurveda and Buddhism
IV. Implementation gap in India's SCO engagement   ->   D. UNESCO Register of Good Safeguarding Practices
questions.explanation: Soft power pillars are Ayurveda and Buddhism, the Games were held in Bishkek, the initiative is in the UNESCO register and the implementation gap is slow progress on payments and corridors.

questions.q:
Read the statements below about India and the SCO:
I. India's SCO vision rests on three pillars: Security, Connectivity and Opportunity.
II. The 6th World Nomad Games 2026 was held in Astana.
III. The Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure treats terror financing and radicalisation as collective regional concerns.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the 2026 Games were held in Bishkek, not Astana.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. The World Nomad Games were first held in 2014.
II. Kok Boru is a traditional Kyrgyz equestrian game in the Nomad Games sports programme.
III. India sent no contingent to the 2026 edition of the Nomad Games.
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while India did send a contingent of 87 members.

quizzes.title: India's SCO ties and outreach
quizzes.passage: India's SCO engagement sits within a broader approach to Eurasia, where access and connectivity matter. Central Asia is landlocked, so institutional links with the region carry particular weight. Energy is another part of the picture, with long-term access to key resources treated as a strategic concern. India's approach also includes cultural outreach aimed at building people-centric ties. The grouping's stated aims include peace, security, stability, economic cooperation and cultural exchange in the region. Digital governance is another area where India's rights-based approach sits in tension with the grouping's focus on data surveillance. Some frictions in the region involve the close ties between two neighbouring countries, and such issues can slow down projects. Practical progress on payment arrangements and transport corridors has been slower than the size of the grouping might suggest. The SCO allows issue-based alignment, so partners can cooperate on specific questions while differing on others. The grouping's agenda covers security, economic and connectivity cooperation, political dialogue, and cultural and people-to-people exchanges. Yet cooperation continues on several fronts, including energy partnerships and green development. The grouping's wider agenda also covers energy, transport, digital economy and environmental protection. India's commitment to peace and stability is stated clearly in its participation, which emphasises dialogue and diplomacy for resolving disputes.

questions.q: Which port, together with the INSTC, reduces dependence on Pakistan-controlled transit for European and Central Asian trade?
questions.explanation: Chabahar Port and the INSTC reduce dependence on Pakistan-controlled transit.

questions.q: In which year was the first edition of the World Nomad Games held?
questions.explanation: The first edition of the World Nomad Games was held in 2014.

questions.q: Which 2012 declaration conceived the World Nomad Games?
questions.explanation: The Games were conceived through the 2012 Bishkek Declaration.

questions.q: Whose register of good safeguarding practices recognises the Nomad Games initiative?
questions.explanation: The Nomad Games initiative is recognised through the UNESCO Register of Good Safeguarding Practices.

questions.q: Which two traditions does India project as soft power pillars?
questions.explanation: India projects Ayurveda and Buddhism as soft power pillars.

questions.q: What is the name of the traditional Kyrgyz game listed in the Nomad Games sports programme?
questions.explanation: Kok Boru is a traditional Kyrgyz equestrian game in the Nomad Games sports programme.

questions.q: India refuses to join which initiative because CPEC passes through disputed territories?
questions.explanation: India refuses the Belt and Road Initiative because CPEC passes through disputed territories.
